messages:
matt_engineer: Quick Q

We're piloting a voluntary "holiday swap pool" on my team so folks can trade holiday days across regions (e.g., trade a US floating holiday for a local EU day). Does company policy allow credits or swaps like that, and how does it affect carryover/tax?

tara_peopleops: Short answer: we can support swaps in principle but they require HR + payroll signoff. Key points: swaps are a bookkeeping/compensation change not a literal "carryover". If you trade a US floating day for an EU regional day we record an equivalent paid day on the receiving entity. That may have tax implications.

matt_engineer: So if I give my US floating holiday to a teammate in London, do I lose that day and they get a paid day? Does that change my vacation balance or carry cap?

olivia_payroll: If it's executed as a swap, payroll will reduce your US holiday entitlement and add an equivalent credit to the UK teammate under the UK entity. For carryover: only vacation balances (not one-off holiday swaps) are considered for the 40h carry cap. But any credit added to the receiving employee that is converted to "vacation" will be subject to that entity's carry rules.

jordan_recruiting: Operationally how would that work for internal candidates or contractors? We sometimes promise a sign-on holiday credit in offers. Can the swap be applied to an offer credit?

tara_peopleops: Offer credits are separate and must be in the offer letter. Swaps should not be used to backfill offer commitments. Contractors are trickier: if the receiving person is a contractor, we cannot add paid holiday to a contractor unless it's in their contract. Contractors converting to FT after a swap will have accruals start on their FT date; any swapped credits given while they were contractors must be addressed case-by-case.

peopleops_bot: Handbook excerpt: "Cross-entity holiday adjustments require HR + Payroll approval; tax and local law may apply. Vacation carryover rules apply only to vacation balances (40h default cap for FT US employees)." https://intranet.redwood/handbook/leave#cross-entity (policy v3.9)

matt_engineer: If we do a swap inside the same legal entity (US->US), can we just transfer the day and avoid tax complications?

olivia_payroll: Internal-entity swaps are simplest: we can reassign the holiday day in our payroll ledger for the same legal entity without tax events beyond normal payroll. Still need written approvals: both employees + managers + HR note. We log as HR adjustment: `HR-ADJ-HOL-<id>`.

matt_engineer: Good. Last piece: comp time vs. carryover. Some EEs asked if we can convert swapped holidays into comp time (bank of hours to use later) that would count toward carryover. Is that allowed?

tara_peopleops: We generally avoid creating ad-hoc comp banks that circumvent carry rules. If you want to convert a holiday into vacation hours for later use, that's effectively creating additional vacation balance and will be subject to carry caps and local law. Submit a formal request describing the reason; HR+Payroll will evaluate.

matt_engineer: Thanks. I'll compile a one-pager with manager approvals and route through HR. Appreciate the clarity.

peopleops_bot: Action items: 1) Matt to create swap one-pager + manager signoffs; 2) HR to open adjustment ticket once received; 3) Payroll to confirm tax/ledger impact. Ticket placeholder: #HOL-SWAP-2201.
